column1: The name should survive Phase 1 (it only answers and guides) and Phase 2 (it acts). Placeholder copy must not promise actions in Phase 1.

column3: Wish-granting helper; already in Jira/branches and the POC.
column4: Brand-neutral, memorable, already socialised with the client. Slightly generic in the AI market.

column2: Ask ASI anything about your property…
column3: Verb-led; the product name is the assistant.
column4: Works as a button label, a ⌘K hint and a voice wake phrase. Very Phase-1-honest (asking, not doing). Less personality.

column3: Hospitality-native metaphor; the concierge knows the hotel and points you to the right place.
column4: Instantly understood by hoteliers; fits Phase 1 (guidance) and grows into Phase 2 (arranges things). Longer word on mobile.

column2: Namaste! Saathi here - what do you need?
column3: Saathi = companion in Hindi/Gujarati; warm and culturally resonant for Indian-American hotel owners without singling out a surname.
column4: Inclusive alternative to 'Patel bhai'; friendly on mobile. Needs a tooltip for non-Indian staff; check trademark.

column2: Kem cho? What can I help with?
column3: Playful nod to the Patel-owned motel community.
column4: Charming for the core customer base but excludes non-Patel owners and most front-line staff; risks reading as a stereotype in an enterprise product; poor fit for a housekeeper's mobile screen. Use, if at all, as an Easter-egg greeting, not the product name.

column3: Brand name as the wake word (cf. 'Hey Siri'); Anand also means 'joy'.
column4: Strong brand tie; natural for voice. Personifies the company, which some owners may find odd; check with ASI leadership.
Zero explanation needed, but heavily associated with Microsoft; weaker hospitality flavour.

column1: Front Desk Genie / Night Auditor's Friend
column3: Role-specific personas on the same brain.
column4: Could be used as contextual sub-labels ('Genie · Housekeeping') rather than separate names - the reference UI already shows 'ASI Genie · Front desk · Harbor View'.

column2: Ask about your property, or say where you want to go…
column3: Ask Genie, or tell it what to do…
column4: Phase 1 must not imply it will perform tasks.
Phase 1 CTAs navigate; Phase 2 CTAs state the exact consequence.

column2: I can't do that yet, but here's the fastest way - I've opened it for you.
column4: Honest, still helpful, keeps trust for Phase 2.

column2: That isn't available for your role. A manager can see it under Dashboard → KPIs.
column4: No data leak, names a path forward.
Role + property always visible - the interaction grammar from the reference UI.

column2: Morning, Alex. 14 arrivals and 9 departures today. Try: Arrivals · Rooms free Friday · How do I split a folio?
column3: Adds: Mark a room clean · Check in Smith
column4: Chips are the discoverability layer and are role-filtered.
